transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I came in because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. I'm a sales rep, so I'm used to being out there, but... it's like the old Ruben who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day is just gone. I just don't feel like myself anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this been going on for weeks, months, or longer?

It's been... I'd say about eight months now. Yeah, definitely months. It started right around the time they brought in a new regional manager at work. He just started coming down on me, taking away accounts I’d handled for years. That's really when all this began.

Before this started eight months ago, have you ever had periods in your life—even if they were shorter or less severe—where you felt depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoyed?

No, I haven't. I mean, everyone has a bad day or a rough week here and there, but... never anything like this. I've always been the kind of guy who just shakes it off and gets back to work. This is really the first time I've ever felt this way.
Besides feeling down and losing interest in things, have you noticed other changes like problems with your sleep, appetite, energy levels, or concentration?

Well, my sleep has definitely been affected. At night, I just lie there in bed, replaying everything from work over and over in my head, just staring at the ceiling. And even when I finally do manage to drift off, I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. I'm already completely worn out by then, and I just lie there dreading the rest of the day.

If you were to leave this job or the regional manager situation were to change, do you think these feelings of emptiness and the sleep problems would go away, or do you feel like this heaviness has become something separate from what's happening at work?

I don't even know anymore. I'd like to think that if I quit, or if he got transferred, I'd go back to normal. But... honestly, I came in today because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It feels like the old Ruben—the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day—is just gone. It feels like it's bigger than just the job now.

Over these past eight months, have there been any stretches of time—even a week or two—when things at work felt less stressful or seemed to improve, and during those periods did your mood and that hollow feeling also improve?

No, not really. Even when things quieted down for a few days—maybe he was out of town or just focused on someone else—I still felt... the same. The stress might have been a little less, but that heavy feeling didn't go away. I still couldn't sleep, still didn't want to do anything. It didn't matter if it was a good week or a bad week at work, I just felt flat either way.

Over these eight months, have you found yourself feeling guilty, blaming yourself, or feeling like you're worthless or a failure—not just about the work situation, but in a more general way about who you are?

Yeah, I have. I just keep telling myself I’m useless now. It’s like... all those years of taking care of my clients and providing for my family, it feels like none of that even counts anymore. Just because I can’t even handle this job now, I feel like a complete failure.

Over these eight months, or even before that, have you ever had stretches of time where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was elevated or unusually good—almost the opposite of how you've been feeling lately?

No, I haven't. I mean, before all this started, I was just... normal. I had regular energy, went to work, slept a normal amount. I've never had a time where I felt unusually high or like I didn't need to sleep. It's pretty much just been the exact opposite of that.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or that life isn't worth living during these past eight months?

Yeah, I have. I've been having these thoughts lately that... well, maybe my wife and kids would just be better off if I didn't wake up. It's hard to admit, but those thoughts scare me. I just don't trust myself the way I used to.

During these past eight months, have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see, or have you had beliefs that felt absolutely true to you but that other people said didn't make sense?

No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen anything that wasn't there. And I don't think I've had any... weird beliefs or anything. Just the depression and the thoughts I mentioned. But no, my mind isn't playing tricks on me like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a Major Depressive Episode of 8 months duration with clear depressive symptoms (depressed mood, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, fatigue, guilt, worthlessness, concentration difficulties, and suicidal ideation). While initiated by a psychosocial stressor (workplace conflict), the depression has become independent of the stressor—symptoms persist even during periods of reduced workplace stress. No history of manic/hypomanic episodes, no psychotic features, and no evidence of trauma meeting PTSD criteria. The persistence and severity of symptoms beyond the initial stressor, combined with the patient's own recognition that the feelings have become 'bigger than just the job,' support a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder rather than an adjustment disorder.
